decisions.why: 味噌汁 (みそしる) is a lexicalized compound; 味噌の汁 is not what natives say for the dish, and the explanation compounds the damage by teaching the の link as the grammar point. Since gen=true the jp may be re-authored, so I fixed jp plus kana, romaji, the literal and both explanations in one pass; the token list still shows 味噌/の/汁 and must be re-parsed from the new jp downstream, since token surface forms are not an editable path here.

edits.new: 朝は味噌汁を飲みます
あさわみそしるをのみます
asawamisoshiruonomimasu

は marks 朝 ('morning') as the topic (the setting being talked about), and を marks 味噌汁 ('miso soup') as the object of 飲む ('to drink/to have'). 味噌汁 is a fixed compound (味噌 'miso' + 汁 'broth'), written with no の between the two parts. 飲みます is the polite present/habitual form. The vocabulary focus is 味噌 ('miso'). In Japanese, soup is 'drunk' (飲む), which is why we use 'to have' in English.

は marca 朝 ('manhã') como o tópico (o cenário sobre o qual se fala), e を marca 味噌汁 ('sopa de missô') como objeto de 飲む ('beber/tomar'). 味噌汁 é um composto fixo (味噌 'missô' + 汁 'caldo'), escrito sem nenhum の entre as duas partes. 飲みます é a forma polida no presente/habitual. O foco do vocabulário é 味噌 ('missô'). Em japonês, sopa se 'bebe' (飲む), por isso usamos 'tomar' em pt-BR.
As for the morning (は), miso soup (を), I drink (polite form).
Quanto à manhã (は), sopa de missô (を), tomo (forma polida).

edits.new: 背中がいたいので病院に行く
せなかがいたいのでびょういんにいく
senakagaitainodebyouinniiku
せなか
senaka

The sentence chains a cause and a consequence using ので ('because/since'). The first part 背中がいたい ('my back hurts') is the reason; the second 病院に行く ('I am going to the hospital') is the result. The parser split ので into の + で, but it functions as a single unit: the causal conjunction ので, which links the two ideas naturally and a little more softly than から.

A frase encadeia uma causa e uma consequência usando ので ('porque/como'). A primeira parte 背中がいたい ('as costas doem') é o motivo; a segunda 病院に行く ('vou ao hospital') é o resultado. O analisador separou ので em の + で, mas funciona como uma unidade só: a conjunção causal ので, que liga as duas ideias de forma natural e um pouco mais suave que から.

母 without honorific is the humble term for the speaker's own mother, so 'a sua mãe' inverts the referent; the finding's 'current' snippet was stale but the defect is real in translation.pt-BR. The same inversion was present in translation.en, translation_literal (both locales) and in the explanation's rationale, so all of them were corrected together to keep the record internally consistent.

edits.new: Alô, a mamãe está em casa?
Hello, is my mom home?
Hello, as for my mother, is she at home?
Alô, quanto à minha mãe, na casa ela está?

After もしもし (hello), the topic is 母は (my mother), marked by は. Then comes 家に, where に indicates the place of existence, and the verb いる ('to be/exist', for living beings) in the polite form います. The final か makes the question. Note that 母 without an honorific always refers to the speaker's own mother, and is the form used when talking about her to people outside the family; to ask about the listener's mother you would say お母さん. The focus is asking whether someone is at home over the phone.

Após もしもし (alô), o tópico é 母は (a minha mãe), marcado por は. Depois vem 家に, onde に indica o local de existência, e o verbo いる ('estar/existir', para seres vivos) na forma polida います. O か final faz a pergunta. Note que 母 sem honorífico se refere sempre à mãe de quem fala, e é a forma usada ao falar dela com pessoas de fora da família; para perguntar pela mãe do interlocutor, usa-se お母さん. O foco é perguntar se alguém está em casa pelo telefone.

edits.new: お金をためて、そうして車を買った

The sentence has two actions linked in sequence. The first, お金をためて (to save money), is in the て form, which here indicates 'I did this, and...'. Then comes そうして ('and so / and then'), reinforcing the idea of consequence, and finally 車を買った (I bought a car), in the past. The focus is the word ためる ('to save/set aside money') within a chain of actions.

A frase tem duas ações ligadas em sequência. A primeira, お金をためて (juntar dinheiro), está na forma て, que aqui indica 'fiz isto, e...'. Depois vem そうして ('e aí / e então'), reforçando a ideia de consequência, e finalmente 車を買った (comprei um carro), no passado. O foco é o vocábulo ためる ('juntar/economizar') dentro de uma cadeia de ações.

decisions.why: With the pure existence verb いる the location is marked by に (狭い駅に人がたくさんいる); で marks the place of an action or event, so で+いる here is ungrammatical for plain existence. The reading change cascades to kana, romaji and the token's r/romaji.

狭い is 'cramped/narrow', not 'crowded' (混んでいる), and the JP carries no demonstrative, so 'this' was invented. The pt translation carried the same invented deictic ('nesta'), so it is aligned in the same edit set.
The old text taught a false grammar fact (で as the marker of place of existence); with the corrected jp the explanation must state that に marks where something exists with いる/ある.
Same false claim in Portuguese, and it is the learner-facing locale, so it gets the identical correction to に.

狭い駅 is an i-adjective directly modifying the following noun: 'cramped station'. The particle に marks the place where something exists (used with いる/ある). 人がたくさんいる says that 'many people exist', with いる being the verb of existence for living beings and たくさん the adverb of quantity.

狭い駅 é um adjetivo-i modificando diretamente o substantivo seguinte: 'estação apertada'. A partícula に marca o lugar onde algo existe (usada com いる/ある). 人がたくさんいる diz que 'muita gente existe', com いる sendo o verbo de existência para seres vivos e たくさん o advérbio de quantidade.

edits.new: The structure is "A に B を 足す": スープに (into the soup) is the destination, 塩を (salt) is the object, and 足した is the verb 足す in the past. The 〜た at the end turns 足す into the past form (足した), indicating an already completed action.
A estrutura é "A に B を 足す": スープに (na sopa) é o destino, 塩を (sal) é o objeto, e 足した é o verbo 足す no passado. O 〜た no fim transforma 足す em forma passada (足した), indicando uma ação já concluída.

edits.new: ここはとても静かだ

Sentence of the type 「X は Y だ」, which describes the topic. ここは establishes the topic (this place), とても is an intensity adverb (very), and 静か is a na-adjective (形状詞) meaning silent/quiet. The だ at the end is the casual copula "is", giving the sentence an informal tone.

Frase do tipo 「X は Y だ」, que descreve o tópico. ここは estabelece o tópico (este lugar), とても é um advérbio de intensidade (muito) e 静か é um adjetivo な (形状詞) que significa silencioso/tranquilo. O だ no final é a cópula casual "é", dando à frase um tom informal.

decisions.why: 絵を描く is the standard orthography; leaving the easy kanji 絵 in kana while keeping the much harder 描 is inconsistent and creates a genuine ambiguity with the interjection え. Kana and romaji are unaffected since 絵 reads え.

The note is internal pipeline commentary about the tokenizer and does not belong in learner-facing text. With jp re-authored to 絵 the caveat is moot, so it is deleted outright and the を clause now cites 絵 directly.
Same leak in pt-BR ('o tokenizador rotulou'). Removed, with the を clause pointing straight at 絵 (desenho).

edits.new: 厚い紙に絵を描いた

The sentence follows the basic Japanese order (complements before the verb, which comes last). 厚い紙 is the い-adjective 厚い (thick) directly modifying the noun 紙 (paper). に marks the place where the action takes hold (on the paper), を marks the direct object 絵 (drawing), and the verb 描く (to draw) comes at the end, in the past form 描いた.

A frase segue a ordem japonesa básica (complementos antes do verbo, que vem por último). 厚い紙 é o adjetivo-i 厚い (grosso) modificando diretamente o substantivo 紙 (papel). に marca o lugar onde a ação se fixa (no papel), を marca o objeto direto 絵 (desenho), e o verbo 描く (desenhar) vem no fim, na forma passada 描いた.

edits.new: ここに座ってもいいですか

Here appears the permission-asking pattern 「verb in te-form + も + いい」 (座ってもいい = may sit / it's okay to sit). ここに marks the place where one wants to sit, 座って is the te-form of the verb, も adds the sense of "even (if)", and いいですか politely asks whether it is okay. Together it becomes the polite request "may I sit here?".

Aqui aparece o padrão de pedir permissão 「verbo na forma て + も + いい」 (座ってもいい = pode sentar / está ok sentar). O ここに marca o lugar onde se quer sentar, 座って é a forma て do verbo, も acrescenta o sentido de "mesmo (se)", e いいですか pergunta educadamente se está tudo bem. O conjunto vira o pedido cortês "posso me sentar aqui?".

decisions.why: Negated existence of an animate noun requires いない; 〜はない with a person survives only in literary set phrases (and then typically with 者), so 学生はない is unnatural modern Japanese. kana, romaji, both explanations (which quote はない three times) and the final token's note all cascade, since ない now negates the verb いる rather than standing alone as the existential.

edits.new: この問題が解けない学生はいない
このもんだいがとけないがくせいわいない
konomondaigatokenaigakuseiwainai

The sentence uses the target pattern 〜ない〜はいない, a double negation that affirms emphatically: 'there is no X that does not...'. First comes a relative clause この問題が解けない ('that cannot solve this problem') that qualifies the noun 学生 ('student'); then 学生は is the topic and the sentence closes with はいない ('there is none'). Because 学生 is a person, existence is negated with いない (from いる), never with ない. The two negations (解けない and はいない) cancel out and the final meaning is positive and emphatic: every student can solve it.

A frase usa o padrão-alvo 〜ない〜はいない, uma dupla negação que afirma de forma enfática: 'não existe X que não...'. Primeiro vem uma oração relativa この問題が解けない ('que não consegue resolver este problema') que qualifica o substantivo 学生 ('estudante'); depois 学生は é o tópico e a frase fecha com はいない ('não existe'). Como 学生 é pessoa, a existência se nega com いない (de いる), nunca com ない. As duas negações (解けない e はいない) se cancelam e o sentido final é positivo e enfático: todo estudante consegue resolvê-lo.
ない here negates the verb いる: いない denies the existence of animate beings (people)
aqui ない nega o verbo いる: いない nega a existência de seres animados (pessoas)

decisions.why: Bare declarative 〜たい is restricted to the speaker (or questions); a third-person subject requires 〜たがる/evidential marking, so 妹はピアノを習いたい teaches a wrong pattern. The recast to 私 keeps the 〜たい teaching target, the topic-は structure and the token count intact (no vocab is declared as the target in the explanation, unlike the お兄さん record), whereas 習いたがっている would silently retarget the whole record.

edits.new: 私はピアノを習いたい
わたしわぴあのをならいたい
watashiwapianoonaraitai
I want to learn the piano.
Quero aprender piano.
As for me, I want to learn piano.

Topic 私は (I) + object ピアノを (piano) + verb in the desiderative 習いたい (want to learn). The 〜たい is formed with the conjunctive stem of the verb (習い) plus the auxiliary たい, which expresses the speaker's own desire; to state a third person's wish you use 〜たがる instead (妹はピアノを習いたがっている). The sentence is casual (ending in たい, without です), so the translation is in a neutral register.

Tópico 私は (eu) + objeto ピアノを (piano) + verbo no desiderativo 習いたい (quero aprender). O 〜たい se forma com a raiz conjuntiva do verbo (習い) mais o auxiliar たい, que exprime o desejo do próprio falante; para afirmar o desejo de outra pessoa, usa-se 〜たがる (妹はピアノを習いたがっている). A frase é casual (termina em たい, sem です), então a tradução fica num registro neutro.

edits.new: Frase curta e coloquial. いくら ('quanto', em quantidade/preço) é um advérbio que indica a quantidade desejada, e ほしい é o adjetivo-i que significa 'querer (ter algo)'. いくら se liga a ほしい de forma adverbial, sem partícula, em qualquer registro (na forma polida: いくらほしいですか). Note que ほしい é um ADJETIVO, não um verbo: literalmente, 'desejado/cobiçado'.

A short, colloquial sentence. いくら ('how much') is an adverb giving the desired quantity, and ほしい is the i-adjective 'to want (to have)'. いくら attaches adverbially, with no particle, in any register (polite: いくらほしいですか). The が of the 〜がほしい pattern would mark the desired object, which here is left unstated (お金が, for instance), never いくら. Intonation (？) does the questioning. ほしい is an ADJECTIVE, not a verb: lit. 'desired/coveted'.

edits.new: 君が怒る ('you getting angry') is nominalized by の, and the predicate is もっともだ ('it's only natural'). The particle も ('also') marks that nominalized clause: besides something already said or implied, your getting angry is understandable too. が marks 君 as the subject inside the clause.

君が怒る ("você ficar bravo") é nominalizado por の, e o predicado é もっともだ ("é natural, compreensível"). A partícula も ("também") marca essa oração nominalizada: além de algo já dito ou subentendido, também é compreensível que você fique bravo. が marca 君 como sujeito interno da oração.

decisions.why: 起こす has both 'wake someone up' and 'give rise to', and with やる気を only the second reading is possible. The en note picked the wrong sense and contradicted the pt-BR note ('fazer despertar') on the same token.

edits.new: auxiliary せる forming the causative おこさせる ("to make (motivation) arise")

decisions.why: 'o alvo alvo' is a duplicated-word typo. Rather than keeping '(o alvo)', which is corpus-build target metadata leaking into learner text and reads as a non sequitur after the gloss 'mas', the parenthetical is removed; the sentence goes on to explain けど anyway.

edits.new: Frase curta e coloquial: o advérbio/interjeição まあ ('bem...', hesitação) abre a fala, seguido do adjetivo いい ('bom, tudo bem') e da partícula けど ('mas'). Aqui けど aparece no fim sem oração seguinte, um uso muito comum em japonês falado para suavizar e deixar a frase 'em aberto', sugerindo uma ressalva não dita ('...mas tem um porém').

decisions.why: Confirmed: the copula 'é' is written without its accent twice, so both clauses read as the conjunction 'e' and the sentences become ungrammatical pt-BR. Purely orthographic fix, no change of content.

edits.new: A frase usa o condicional 〜たら ('se/quando'): 落としたら ('se deixar cair') estabelece a condição. O resultado é 割れる ('quebrar(-se)'), seguido de だろう, que expressa probabilidade/suposição ('provavelmente, deve'). それは é o tópico marcado por は.

decisions.why: 'conetiva' is the European-Portuguese spelling; pt-BR keeps the c, so it must be 'conectiva'. While in the same record I also corrected the stray diaeresis in 'advërbio' -> 'advérbio' in the pt explanation, an unambiguous typo in learner-facing text.

edits.new: raiz conectiva de する (連用形), antes de ます

A frase abre com o conectivo そして, que liga este enunciado ao que veio antes, com sentido de 'e' / 'e então'. O tópico 男の子 (o menino) é marcado por は, e o predicado そうしました ('fez assim') usa o advérbio そう ('assim') seguido do verbo する no passado polido (しました). É a estrutura típica de そして no início de frase, encadeando ações narrativas.

decisions.why: Confirmed: 'automatica' lacks the required accent ('automática') and the copula 'é' in 'ゼリーは e o tópico' is missing its accent. Note that the earlier 'natural e automática' keeps the unaccented 'e' because there it really is the conjunction.

edits.new: A frase usa o condicional/temporal 〜と, que indica consequência natural e automática ('sempre que/quando X, então Y'). 冷えると ('quando esfria') leva a 固くなる ('fica dura'): adjetivo 固い na forma adverbial 固く + なる ('tornar-se'). ゼリーは é o tópico marcado por は.
A gelatina, quando esfria, dura fica.

decisions.why: Confirmed: the parenthesis opened before 'literally' is closed only after the final clause, so the whole すぐに remark is swallowed into the gloss aside and the period lands inside the parentheses. The pt version has the identical garbling, so both were repunctuated together to keep the record consistent.

edits.new: The focus is 〜たほうがいい, used to give a piece of advice ('it's better to do X'). The structure is: verb in the short past form (寝た, from 寝る) + ほう ('side/option') + が + いい ('good') (literally 'the option of sleeping is the good one'). The adverb すぐ + に at the beginning means 'immediately, right now', reinforcing the urgency of the advice.

O foco é 〜たほうがいい, usado para dar um conselho ('é melhor fazer X'). A estrutura é: verbo na forma passada curta (寝た, de 寝る) + ほう ('lado/opção') + が + いい ('bom') (literalmente 'a opção de dormir é a boa'). O advérbio すぐ + に no início significa 'imediatamente, já', reforçando a urgência do conselho.

decisions.why: Confirmed, and the defect is in the note rather than the role. In あるわけがない the ある is the existential verb in attributive (連体形) position modifying わけ, not the 連体詞 ある ('a certain'), so 'determinante' contradicts both the token's own role ('verbo principal') and the sentence explanation. The role text itself is correct and stays.

edits.new: forma de dicionário de ある em posição atributiva (連体形) diante de わけ
dictionary (attributive) form of the verb ある modifying わけ

decisions.why: 当たり (あたり) is three morae, so calling it the 'last syllable' is factually wrong; the pedagogical point survives with 'a noun that ends in 当たり'. The pt-BR mirror carries the identical false claim ('última sílaba'), so it is corrected in the same edit set to keep the record consistent.

edits.new: The target focus was 〜たりする, but it does NOT appear here. 八つ当たり ('to take it out on / vent one's anger on someone who is not to blame') is a noun that ends in 当たり; the 'たり' is part of that word, not the listing grammar. The real structure is 八つ当たり + する ('to do/commit a 八つ当たり') + な (prohibition) + よ (emphasis): 'don't take it out on me!'.

O foco alvo era 〜たりする, mas ele NÃO aparece aqui. 八つ当たり ('descontar/descarregar a raiva em quem não tem culpa') é um substantivo que termina em 当たり; o 'たり' faz parte dessa palavra, não da gramática de listagem. A estrutura real é 八つ当たり + する ('fazer/cometer um 八つ当たり') + な (proibição) + よ (ênfase): 'não desconte em mim!'.

decisions.why: The defect is real: じゃ here is the first half of plain negation じゃない (= ではない), not the tag-question 'isn't it', and the explanation itself stresses this is the genuine negating use. Note the finding's index is off by one: the quoted current value "(part of 'isn't it')" lives on token 5 (じゃ), not token 6 (ない, whose gloss 'is not' is already correct), so the edit is emitted at tokens[5].gloss.en.

edits.new: (part of 'is not')

decisions.why: Confirmed critical grammar error: existential いる is animate-only and cannot take the inanimate ピザ as its subject, so the verb must be 要る ('to need/want'), giving ピザがいる人 = 'person who needs/wants pizza'. The current text teaches a false rule about がいる and invents a 'person for whom there is pizza' reading.

Same false analysis in the learner-facing language ('existir, para seres vivos' with an inanimate subject). Rewritten to name 要る explicitly and to state that the target pattern がいる is not what actually occurs here.

edits.new: The target pattern was the existential がいる, but that is not what appears here. With the inanimate subject ピザ, いる is the verb 要る ('to need, to want'), whose object is marked by が: ピザがいる人 = 'a person who needs/wants pizza'. Existential いる is only for living beings and could never take ピザ as its subject. The whole relative clause modifies the noun 人 (person). It is a colloquial call, with さあ opening it and the lengthening ー at the end sounding like a shout to the group.

O padrão-alvo era o がいる de existência, mas não é ele que aparece aqui. Com o sujeito inanimado ピザ, いる é o verbo 要る ('precisar, querer'), cujo objeto vem marcado por が: ピザがいる人 = 'pessoa que precisa/quer pizza'. O いる de existência serve só para seres vivos e nunca poderia ter ピザ como sujeito. Toda a oração relativa modifica o substantivo 人 (pessoa). É uma chamada coloquial, com さあ no começo e o alongamento ー no fim soando como um grito para a turma.
to need, to want (要る)
precisar, querer (要る)
dictionary form of 要る (written in kana here), modifying the following noun
forma de dicionário de 要る (escrito em kana aqui), modificando o substantivo seguinte
Well, the person who needs (wants) pizza (!)

decisions.why: Both typos are real: 'não faca' lacks the cedilla ('não faça') and 'este な final e a partícula' loses the copula accent, turning the clause into a fragment ('é'). The same 'não-faca' typo also appears in translation_literal.pt-BR, so it is fixed in the same edit set.

edits.new: Frase de proibição: o verbo na forma de dicionário 投げる recebe a partícula final な, que forma o imperativo negativo (uma ordem forte de 'não faça'). 犬に indica o alvo da ação (em quem se joga) e 石を o objeto jogado. Cuidado: este な final é a partícula de proibição, diferente do な de adjetivos-na.
Cachorro [alvo] pedra [objeto] jogar não-faça!

decisions.why: The duplication '(o alvo/alvo da frase)' is a clear slip. The finding also asks for the 'analisador' meta-note to be rephrased: a reference to the pipeline's morphological analyzer and its wrong English hint is corpus-build metadata that must not sit in learner-facing text, so both languages now state the useful contrast directly (root is 済む, not 住む) without naming the tooling, and the pt 'o analisador separou' becomes a neutral statement about the split.

edits.new: すみません é uma expressão fixa de pedido de desculpas; com o ponto final 「。」 soa como um 'desculpe' calmo. Historicamente vem do verbo 済む (sumu, 'ficar resolvido/quitado') na forma negativa polida 済みません ('não fica quitado', isto é, 'não consigo me sentir em paz com isto'), por isso a divisão em すみ + ませ + ん. Para o iniciante, porém, o melhor é decorá-la inteira como fórmula de desculpa (o alvo da frase). Atenção: a raiz é 済む ('ficar resolvido'), não 住む ('morar').

すみません is a fixed expression for apologizing; with the period '。' it sounds like a calm 'sorry'. Historically it comes from the verb 済む (sumu, 'to be settled/paid off') in the polite negative form 済みません ('it isn't settled', that is, 'I can't feel at peace about this'), which is why it splits into すみ + ませ + ん. For the beginner, however, it is best to memorize it whole as an apology formula (the target of the sentence). Careful: the root is 済む ('to be settled'), not 住む ('to live').

decisions.why: Etymology is stated backwards: おめでとう is the u-onbin form of お + めでたく, so it derives FROM めでたい rather than being its origin. Fixed in en and in the pt mirror ('origem do adjetivo' to 'derivada do adjetivo'), as the finding requests.

Self-contradictory as written: ございます already contains ます, so ます cannot attach to it; it attaches to ござい, the 連用形 stem of ござる, exactly as the token note on index 1 states. Fixed in en and in the identical pt wording, with 'ele descreve' disambiguated to 'o padrão ます descreve'.

edits.new: Fixed expression of congratulation. おめでとう is an interjection (derived from the adjective めでたい, 'auspicious'), and ございます is the polite form of ござる, which here functions as an honorific copula equivalent to です/あります. Notice that ます (the polite verb ending) attaches to ござい, the stem of ござる, within a crystallized formula; the ます pattern describes the polite conjugation of full verbs, not this fixed greeting.

Expressão fixa de felicitação. おめでとう é uma interjeição (derivada do adjetivo めでたい, 'auspicioso'), e ございます é a forma polida de ござる, que aqui funciona como cópula honorífica equivalente a です/あります. Repare que ます (terminação polida de verbo) se anexa a ござい, a raiz de ござる, dentro de uma fórmula cristalizada; o padrão ます descreve a conjugação polida de verbos plenos, e não esta saudação fixa.

decisions.why: The finding's premise is factually wrong: there are no null カップ/ケーキ subtokens at indices 0-1 — index 0 IS the combined カップケーキ (the glossed token) and index 1 is 型. Concatenating all ten surfaces yields カップケーキ型に、ペーパーカップを並べます。 exactly, so jp alignment is already correct and removing any token would break it.

つながわ is not a real form; the 未然形 of the godan verb つなぐ is つなが, which combines with the passive auxiliary れる to give つながれる. The typo appears identically in both locales and would teach a nonexistent conjugation base.

decisions.why: '(ださ)' is not a form of ござる at all; the 連用形 that attaches to 〜ます is ござい, which is precisely this token's own surface. Leaving it would contradict the token the note annotates.

forma 連用形 (ござい) de ござる, base para receber 〜ます

decisions.why: The English explanation is cut off mid-word ("means 'l..."), so the entire account of 〜のように is missing. The pt-BR version is complete, so the fix is to restore the English to mirror it, including the comparison-vs-purpose contrast.

edits.new: The sentence has the topic 彼女は (as for her) and ends with the noun-adjective 親切だ (is kind). The stretch 天使のように means 'like an angel': here 〜のように compares her to an angel and works as an adverb modifying 'kind'. The adverb とても (very) reinforces the intensity. Note that this 〜ように is the COMPARISON use ('like'), not the purpose one.

Corpus-build metadata must never appear in learner content, so the note is rewritten to state only the grammatical fact: し is the stem of する in the compound verb 自殺する.

decisions.why: The explanation is learner-facing and must not carry build-pipeline commentary; 'the analyzer joined みな and そこ into a single block' describes our tooling, not Japanese grammar. Replaced with a plain statement that みな and そこ are two separate words, keeping the へ/destination teaching point intact.
Same tooling meta-commentary in pt-BR ('o analisador juntou みな e そこ num só bloco'). Rewritten in parallel with the en version so both locales say the same thing without referring to the corpus build.

The merge is a real defect: みな ('todos') and そこ ('lá', the destination of へ) are independent words. A true token split is not expressible in the allowed edit paths, which only reach fields of an existing token, so I applied the fully expressible part: gloss, role and note now name the two components cleanly and no longer contain the 'bloco mal segmentado / poorly segmented block' QA remark, which is corpus-build metadata that must not reach a learner.

edits.new: The sentence shows the target へ: the direction particle へ marks そこ ('there') as the destination of the movement, forming 〜へ行く ('to go to'). The topic is 彼ら ('they'), marked by は, and みな ('all') reinforces that it is all of them. The verb is 行く (godan/う), here in the simple past いった ('went'). みな and そこ are two separate words: みな ('all') restates 彼ら as a whole, and そこ ('there') is the destination marked by へ.

A frase mostra o alvo へ: a partícula de direção へ marca そこ ('lá') como o destino do movimento, formando 〜へ行く ('ir para'). O tópico é 彼ら ('eles'), marcado por は, e みな ('todos') reforça que se trata de todos eles. O verbo é 行く (godan/う), aqui no passado simples いった ('foram'). みな e そこ são duas palavras separadas: みな ('todos') retoma 彼ら como um conjunto, e そこ ('lá') é o destino marcado por へ.
all + there (みな 'all' + そこ 'there')
todos + lá (みな 'todos' + そこ 'lá')
みな ('todos'), que retoma 彼ら, seguido de そこ ('lá'), destino marcado por へ
This block holds two words: みな ('all'), which refers back to 彼ら, and そこ ('there'), the destination marked by へ.
Este bloco reúne duas palavras: みな ('todos'), que retoma 彼ら, e そこ ('lá'), o destino marcado por へ.
